Name: Saint Mary, Mother of Jesus
Major_Events: Annunciation by the angel Gabriel
Birth of Jesus in Bethlehem
Presentation of Jesus at the Temple
Witnessed the Crucifixion of Jesus
Present at the Resurrection and Ascension
Notable_Contributions: Mother of Jesus Christ, the Savior
Role in salvation history as Theotokos (Mother of God)
Inspiration for Marian devotion and theology
Quotes: "I am the handmaid of the Lord. Let it be done unto me according to your word."
Vocation_Job: Mother of Jesus, Devotee of God

Name: Saint Michael the Archangel
Major_Events: Led God's armies in the battle against Lucifer
Intervened to end a plague in Rome at Pope Gregory I's request
Protected the church at Colossae from destruction
Apparition on Mount Gargano in 492
Notable_Contributions: Defender of the Faith and leader of the Church Militant
Interceded for humanity during critical moments in history
Inspired devotion and numerous pilgrimage sites such as Mont Saint-Michel
Quotes: "Who is like God?"

Name: Saint Joseph
Major_Events: Received divine messages in dreams
Protected Mary and Jesus during the flight into Egypt
Cared for and raised Jesus as his earthly father
Provided for the Holy Family through his carpentry work
Notable_Contributions: Model of fatherhood and family life
Patron and protector of the Universal Church
Exemplar of obedience to God’s will
Sanctified daily labor as a carpenter
Conversion_Status: Lifelong Jew and follower of God

Name: Saint Peter the Apostle
Major_Events: Called by Jesus to be an Apostle
Renamed 'Peter' (meaning 'Rock') by Jesus
First to declare Jesus as the Christ
Leader at Pentecost and early Church
Crucified upside-down under Emperor Nero
Notable_Contributions: First Pope of the Roman Catholic Church
Established the Church in Rome
Preacher and missionary to Jews and Gentiles
Performed miracles in the name of Jesus
Advocated for Gentile inclusion at the Council of Jerusalem
Quotes: Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life.

Name: Saint Paul the Apostle
Major_Events: Conversion on the road to Damascus
Three missionary journeys across Asia Minor, Greece, and Rome
Council of Jerusalem
Imprisonments in Rome and elsewhere
Notable_Contributions: Authored significant portions of the New Testament
Spread Christianity to the Gentiles
Shaped Christian theology and Christology
Established Christian communities across the Roman Empire
Quotes: "I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me."
"For to me, to live is Christ and to die is gain."
"Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud."
Vocation_Job: Apostle, Missionary, Tent Maker, Theologian, Writer

Name: Saint John the Apostle
Major_Events: Called to be an Apostle by Jesus in the first year of His public ministry
Witnessed the Transfiguration of Jesus
Present at the Last Supper and leaned on Jesus’ chest
Stood at the foot of the Cross and was entrusted with the care of Mary, the Mother of Jesus
Ministered in Ephesus and Asia Minor
Exiled to the Island of Patmos where he wrote the Book of Revelation
Authored the Gospel of John and three Epistles
Notable_Contributions: Authored the Gospel of John
Wrote three Epistles in the New Testament
Wrote the Book of Revelation
Played a key role in the early Christian Church
Cared for the Virgin Mary after Jesus’ crucifixion
Quotes: God is love, and whoever abides in love abides in God, and God abides in them.

Name: Saint Andrew the Apostle
Major_Events: First disciple called by Jesus
Introduced his brother Peter to Jesus
Participated in the miracle of the feeding of the 5,000
Evangelized in regions including Scythia, Greece, and Turkey
Martyred in Patras on an X-shaped cross
Notable_Contributions: Spread Christianity to regions around the Black Sea
Established Christian churches and ordained clergy
Symbolism of the St. Andrew's Cross
Quotes: "Accept me, O Christ Jesus, whom I saw, whom I love, and in whom I am; accept my spirit in peace in your eternal realm."

Name: Saint James the Greater
Major_Events: Witnessed the Transfiguration of Jesus
Was among the inner circle of Jesus alongside Peter and John
Preached Christianity in the Iberian Peninsula
Beheaded by King Herod Agrippa I in Jerusalem
Notable_Contributions: Spread Christianity in Spain
First apostle to be martyred
Inspiration for the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage
Quotes: In the name of Jesus Christ, for whom I am being led to execution, stand up and bless your Creator.

Name: Saint James the Less
Major_Events: Witnessed the Resurrection of Christ
Served as the first Bishop of Jerusalem
Participated in the Council of Jerusalem (circa AD 50)
Notable_Contributions: Author of the first Catholic Epistle (Epistle of James)
Guided the early Christian Church in Jerusalem
Advocated for the inclusion of Gentiles in Christianity without requiring adherence to Mosaic Law

Name: Saint Thomas the Apostle
Major_Events: Witnessed the Resurrection of Christ and professed, 'My Lord and My God'
Evangelized in Syria, Persia, and India
Established seven churches in Kerala, India
Performed miracles, including raising the dead
Notable_Contributions: Spread Christianity to India
Converted kings and their families to Christianity
Built churches and established Christian communities in southern India
Quotes: My Lord and My God.

Name: Saint Philip the Apostle
Major_Events: Called directly by Jesus to follow Him
Participated in the miracle of the loaves and fishes
Preached and evangelized across Greece, Phrygia, and Syria
Converted the proconsul's wife in Hierapolis
Notable_Contributions: Introduced Nathanael to Christ
Spread Christianity throughout Asia Minor
Performed miracles to confirm the Gospel's message
Died as a martyr in Hierapolis, inspiring faith in early Christians
Quotes: Lord, show us the Father, and it is enough for us.

Name: Saint Bartholomew the Apostle
Major_Events: One of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus
Witnessed Christ's Ascension
Missionary work in India, Armenia, Mesopotamia, Persia, and Egypt
Translated the Gospel of Matthew into a local language in India
Martyred for converting King Polymius of Armenia to Christianity
Notable_Contributions: Spread Christianity to India and Armenia
Left a copy of the Gospel of Matthew in India
Converted King Polymius and his family to Christianity
Credited with numerous miracles, including healing King Polymius' daughter
Quotes: "Here is a true Israelite in whom there is no deceit."

Name: Saint Matthew the Apostle
Major_Events: Called by Jesus to be one of the Twelve Apostles
Authored the Gospel of Matthew
Witnessed Christ's resurrection and ascension
Notable_Contributions: Wrote the Gospel of Matthew, emphasizing Jesus as the Messiah
Spread Christianity in regions including Ethiopia, Parthia, and Persia
Helped establish early Christian communities
Quotes: Follow me.

Name: Saint Simon the Zealot
Historical_Death_Place: Suanir, Persia (traditional) or various locations including Jerusalem or Edessa
Major_Events: Witnessed the miracle at Cana
Evangelized in Persia, Egypt, and Africa
Received the Holy Spirit at Pentecost
Notable_Contributions: Spread Christianity to various regions including Persia and Africa
Helped establish early Christian communities
Served as an example of zealous faith and loyalty

Name: Saint Jude Thaddeus
Major_Events: Preached the Gospel in Judea, Samaria, and beyond
Wrote the Epistle of Jude warning against false teachings
Evangelized in Mesopotamia, Libya, and Persia alongside St. Simon
Credited with helping establish the Armenian Church
Notable_Contributions: Author of the Epistle of Jude in the New Testament
Healed King Abgar V of Edessa
Spread Christianity beyond the Roman Empire
Quotes: "May mercy, peace, and love be yours in abundance." (Jude 1:2)

Name: Saint Matthias the Apostle
Major_Events: Chosen to replace Judas Iscariot as an Apostle
Witnessed the Resurrection of Jesus
Preached in Cappadocia, Ethiopia, and regions around the Caspian Sea
Notable_Contributions: Evangelized various regions including Cappadocia and Ethiopia
Became one of the Twelve Apostles, completing their number after Judas' betrayal
Quotes: "The harvest is abundant but the laborers are few; so ask the master of the harvest to send out laborers for his harvest." (Luke 10:2, attributed to his mission)

Name: Saint Stephen the Martyr
Major_Events: Ordained as one of the first deacons of the Church
Delivered a powerful speech before the Sanhedrin recounting salvation history
Stoned to death for proclaiming Jesus as the Son of God
Notable_Contributions: First Christian martyr (Protomartyr)
Model of forgiveness, praying for his persecutors at death
Inspired early Christians with his faith and witness
Quotes: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.
Lord, do not hold this sin against them.

Name: Saint Barnabas
Major_Events: Joined the Jerusalem church after Christ's resurrection
Sold his property and donated all proceeds to the apostles
Introduced Paul to the apostles in Jerusalem
Preached in Antioch where followers were first called 'Christians'
Undertook missionary journeys with Paul
Participated in the Council of Jerusalem to resolve disputes over Gentile converts
Notable_Contributions: Helped establish the Church in Antioch
Evangelized among Gentiles
Strengthened early Christian communities
Promoted unity and reconciliation within the Church

Name: Saint Luke the Evangelist
Major_Events: Accompanied St. Paul on missionary journeys
Authored the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles
Witnessed key events in early Christianity, including the road to Emmaus encounter
Ordained as Bishop of Thebes
Notable_Contributions: Authored over 25% of the New Testament
Wrote the Gospel of Luke, emphasizing social justice and salvation for all
Chronicled the actions of the Apostles in the Acts of the Apostles
Traditionally credited as the first Christian iconographer
Quotes: Blessed are the poor.

Name: Saint Mark the Evangelist
Major_Events: Authored the Gospel of Mark
Companion of St. Peter and St. Paul
Founded the Church in Alexandria
Served as the first Bishop of Alexandria
Notable_Contributions: Wrote the Gospel of Mark, the earliest and shortest Gospel
Established Christianity in Africa through his mission in Alexandria
Created the theological school in Alexandria
Quotes: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ the Son of God.

Name: Saint Mary Magdalene
Historical_Death_Place: Possibly Ephesus, Roman Province of Asia
Major_Events: Healed by Jesus who cast out seven demons
Witnessed the Crucifixion of Christ
First to witness the Resurrection of Christ
Proclaimed the Resurrection to the Apostles
Notable_Contributions: First witness to the Resurrection of Jesus
Proclaimed the Good News of the Resurrection
Example of repentance and deep faith
Quotes: I have seen the Lord.

Name: Saint Augustine of Hippo
Major_Events: Converted to Christianity under the influence of St. Ambrose
Baptized in 387 along with his son Adeodatus
Became Bishop of Hippo in 395
Combated Manichaeism, Donatism, and Pelagianism
Wrote influential works like 'Confessions' and 'The City of God'
Notable_Contributions: Formulated the doctrine of original sin
Developed just war theory
Authored over five million words on theology and philosophy
Provided foundational contributions to Western Christianity and philosophy
Quotes: You have made us for yourself, O Lord, and our heart is restless until it rests in you.
Faith is to believe what you do not see; the reward of this faith is to see what you believe.

Name: Saint Ambrose of Milan
Major_Events: Became Bishop of Milan in 374 by popular acclamation
Fought against Arianism and defended Nicene Christianity
Baptized and mentored Saint Augustine of Hippo
Excommunicated Emperor Theodosius I after the Thessalonica massacre
Introduced Ambrosian hymns and church music practices
Notable_Contributions: Defended Church independence from state control
Wrote influential theological works like 'De Fide' and 'De Officiis Ministrorum'
Promoted the Christianization of the Roman Empire
Contributed to early church-state relations
Quotes: "When I am at Rome, I fast on a Saturday; when I am at Milan, I do not. Follow the custom of the church where you are."
"The emperor is in the Church, not above the Church."
"If the Church has gold it is not to protect it, but to give it to those in need."
Vocation_Job: Bishop, Theologian, Statesman, Church Father, Doctor of the Church

Name: Saint Jerome
Modern_Birthplace: Stridon, likely in Croatia or Slovenia
Major_Events: Baptized by Pope Liberius in 366
Lived as a hermit in the Desert of Chalcis for four years
Ordained as a priest in Antioch under the condition of pursuing monastic life
Served as secretary to Pope Damasus I
Translated the Bible into Latin, known as the Vulgate
Established a monastery, convents, and a hostel in Bethlehem
Notable_Contributions: Translation of the Bible into Latin (the Vulgate)
Defended the perpetual virginity of Mary
Wrote extensive biblical commentaries and theological works
Promoted monasticism and asceticism
Quotes: Ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ.
Let holy reading be always at hand. Sleep may fall upon thee as thou lookest thereon, and the sacred page find thy face downcast.
Be ever engaged, so that whenever the devil calls he may find you occupied.
Vocation_Job: Priest, Theologian, Translator, Biblical Scholar, Monk

Name: Saint Gregory the Great
Major_Events: Elected as Pope on 590-09-03
Initiated the Gregorian Mission to England in 597
Reorganized the papal treasury to aid the poor and victims of famine
Introduced liturgical reforms influencing Gregorian chant
Articulated the doctrine of Purgatory
Notable_Contributions: Reasserted papal authority across Europe
Expanded missionary work, particularly to the Anglo-Saxons
Reformed Church liturgy and administration
Authored influential theological works including 'Pastoral Rule' and 'Moralia on Job'
Quotes: The only true riches are those that make us rich in virtue.

Popes.Pontifical_Motto: Servus Servorum Dei (Servant of the Servants of God)

Name: Saint Thomas Aquinas
Major_Events: Joined the Dominican Order in 1244
Authored 'Summa Theologiae' and 'Summa Contra Gentiles'
Taught at the University of Paris
Advised Popes and participated in theological debates
Canonized in 1323 by Pope John XXII
Notable_Contributions: Developed the synthesis of faith and reason
Authored theological and philosophical works including 'Summa Theologiae'
Established the Five Ways (proofs for the existence of God)
Incorporated Aristotelian philosophy into Christian theology
Composed hymns such as 'Tantum Ergo Sacramentum' and 'Adoro Te Devote'
Quotes: To one who has faith, no explanation is necessary. To one without faith, no explanation is possible.
The things that we love tell us what we are.

Name: Saint Francis of Assisi
Major_Events: Founded the Franciscan Order in 1209
Received the stigmata in 1224
Canonized on July 16, 1228 by Pope Gregory IX
Established the Poor Clares and the Third Order of Franciscans
Notable_Contributions: Promoted evangelical poverty and devotion to Christ
Inspired the Franciscan movement, one of the largest religious orders
Wrote the 'Canticle of the Creatures', a hymn celebrating creation
Introduced the first living Nativity scene
Quotes: This is what I wish; this is what I am seeking. This is what I want to do from the bottom of my heart.
Praise be to you, my Lord, through our Sister, Mother Earth, who sustains and governs us.

Name: Saint Dominic
Major_Events: Founded the Order of Preachers, commonly known as the Dominicans, in 1216
Established the first Dominican convent at Prouille, France in 1206
Engaged in preaching missions against the Cathar heresy in southern France
Received papal approval for the Dominican Order from Pope Honorius III in 1216
Canonized as a saint by Pope Gregory IX in 1234
Notable_Contributions: Founded the Dominican Order, emphasizing intellectual study and preaching
Promoted the reform of religious orders and theological education
Advocated for a life of poverty and simplicity among preachers
Spread the use of the rosary as an important Marian devotion
Quotes: Arm yourself with prayer rather than a sword; wear humility rather than fine clothes.
Vocation_Job: Priest, Founder of the Dominican Order, Theologian

Name: Saint Benedict of Nursia
Major_Events: Founded twelve monasteries at Subiaco
Established the monastery at Monte Cassino
Formulated the Rule of Saint Benedict
Notable_Contributions: Considered the Father of Western Monasticism
Developed the Benedictine Rule, a foundational text for monastic life
Established principles of communal prayer, manual labor, and spiritual growth
Quotes: Idleness is the enemy of the soul.
He who labors as he prays lifts his heart to God.
Vocation_Job: Monk, Abbot, Theologian, Founder of Western Monasticism

Name: Saint Scholastica
Historical_Death_Place: Near Monte Cassino, Kingdom of Italy
Major_Events: Founded the first convent of Benedictine nuns near Monte Cassino
Annual spiritual meetings with her brother, Saint Benedict
Legendary prayer for a storm to converse longer with Saint Benedict
Notable_Contributions: Established Benedictine monastic life for women
Advocated for the contemplative dimension of monasticism
Inspired the spread of convent schools and education for women
Quotes: When I appealed to you, you would not listen to me. So I turned to my God and He heard my prayer.

Name: Saint Clare of Assisi
Historical_Birthplace: Assisi, Duchy of Spoleto, Holy Roman Empire
Historical_Death_Place: Assisi, Duchy of Spoleto, Holy Roman Empire
Major_Events: Founded the Order of Poor Ladies (later known as the Poor Clares) in 1212
Defended Assisi from invaders with the Blessed Sacrament in 1244
Received a vision of Mass while bedridden, leading to her patronage of television
Wrote the first monastic rule for women, approved shortly before her death in 1253
Notable_Contributions: Established a new model of monastic life for women based on poverty and simplicity
Inspired the foundation of 22 monastic houses during her lifetime
Defended the radical commitment to poverty of her order against ecclesiastical opposition
Performed miracles, including healing and protecting her convent from invaders
Quotes: Love God, serve God; everything is in that.
O Lord, protect these Sisters whom I cannot protect now.
They say that we are too poor, but can a heart which possesses the infinite God be truly called poor?

Name: Saint Catherine of Siena
Major_Events: Mystical marriage to Christ at age 21
Advocated for Pope Gregory XI to return the papacy to Rome
Supported Pope Urban VI during the Great Schism
Authored 'The Dialogue of Divine Providence'
Established a monastery for women in Siena
Notable_Contributions: Played a key role in resolving Church political conflicts
Wrote over 400 letters on theology and Church reform
Declared a Doctor of the Church in 1970
Influenced the return of the papacy from Avignon to Rome
Quotes: Be who God meant you to be and you will set the world on fire.
Proclaim the truth and do not be silent through fear.
You are rewarded not according to your work or your time but according to the measure of your love.
Vocation_Job: Mystic, Theologian, Political Advocate, Dominican Tertiary

Name: Saint Teresa of Ávila
Birth_Name: Teresa Sánchez de Cepeda Dávila y Ahumada
Historical_Death_Place: Alba de Tormes, Crown of Castile
Major_Events: Founded the Discalced Carmelite reform in 1562
Established 17 convents for nuns and 15 monasteries with the help of St. John of the Cross
Authored spiritual classics like 'The Interior Castle' and 'The Way of Perfection'
Declared the first female Doctor of the Church in 1970
Notable_Contributions: Reformed the Carmelite Order to restore its original austerity and contemplative focus
Wrote extensively on Christian mysticism and mental prayer, leaving a lasting legacy in theology
Developed a structured guide for spiritual growth in her work 'The Interior Castle'
Quotes: Let nothing perturb you, nothing frighten you. All things pass. God does not change. Patience achieves everything.
It is for you to look at Him, for He never takes His eyes off you.
Lord, either let me suffer or let me die.
Vocation_Job: Carmelite nun, Mystic, Author, Religious Reformer

Name: Saint John of the Cross
Major_Events: Co-founded the Discalced Carmelite reform with St. Teresa of Ávila in 1568
Imprisoned for nine months due to reforms within the Carmelite Order
Wrote significant mystical and spiritual works while in captivity
Played a key role in the establishment and leadership of reformed Carmelite monasteries
Notable_Contributions: Authored profound spiritual and mystical works, including 'Dark Night of the Soul', 'Ascent of Mount Carmel', and 'A Spiritual Canticle'
Reformed the Carmelite Order alongside St. Teresa of Ávila
Influenced Catholic mystical theology and spirituality profoundly
Quotes: Where there is no love, put love, and you will find love.
In the twilight of life, God will not judge us on our earthly possessions and human successes, but on how well we have loved.
To reach where you are not, you have to go through where you are not. To achieve everything, do not want to own anything. To come to be everything, not wanting to be anything.

Name: Saint Ignatius of Loyola
Birth_Name: Íñigo López de Oñaz y Loyola
Historical_Birthplace: Castle Loyola, Guipúzcoa, Crown of Castile
Major_Events: Founded the Society of Jesus in 1540
Published 'Spiritual Exercises' in 1548
Elected the first Superior General of the Jesuits in 1541
Notable_Contributions: Developed Ignatian Spirituality through 'Spiritual Exercises'
Reformative role in the Counter-Reformation
Established Jesuit educational and missionary efforts globally
Quotes: Man was created to praise, reverence and serve God our Lord, and by this means to save his soul.
Vocation_Job: Catholic Priest, Theologian, Founder of the Jesuits

Name: Saint Francis Xavier
Major_Events: Co-founded the Society of Jesus in 1534
Ordained as a priest on June 24, 1537
Missionary work in India, Japan, and the Malay Archipelago
Converted thousands, including baptizing 10,000 in India in late 1544
Died while attempting to enter China for evangelization
Notable_Contributions: Pioneered missionary work in Asia, particularly in India and Japan
Translated the Catechism into local languages
Helped establish Christianity in regions previously untouched by European missionaries
Founded schools and colleges for educating priests and catechists
Quotes: All these dangers and discomforts, when borne for the love of our Lord Jesus Christ, are treasuries filled with heavenly consolations, so much so that one might lose one’s eyesight from weeping so abundantly the sweetest tears of joy.

Name: Saint Aloysius Gonzaga
Historical_Birthplace: Castiglione delle Stiviere, Republic of Venice
Major_Events: Received First Communion from St. Charles Borromeo in 1580
Joined the Society of Jesus in 1585
Renounced his inheritance and title at age 18
Volunteered to serve plague victims in Rome in 1591
Notable_Contributions: Exemplified purity and virtue in a corrupt society
Dedicated his life to teaching catechism and serving the needy
Inspired the establishment of academic institutions in his honor
Quotes: "O Lord, leave me!" (uttered when striving to balance his mystical experiences with obedience to his superiors)

Name: Saint Vincent de Paul
Patron_Of: Society of St. Vincent de Paul
Major_Events: Ordained a priest in 1600
Captured and enslaved by Barbary pirates in 1605, escaped in 1607
Founded the Congregation of the Mission in 1625
Co-founded the Daughters of Charity in 1633
Pioneered seminary education and clergy reform in France
Notable_Contributions: Reformed clergy education and training
Organized widespread charitable works for the poor and sick
Inspired the foundation of the Society of St. Vincent de Paul
Established hospitals and relief missions for the poor
Quotes: The most powerful weapon to conquer the devil is humility. For, as he does not know at all how to employ it, neither does he know how to defend himself from it.
Make it a practice to judge persons and things in the most favorable light at all times and under all circumstances.
We must have a high regard for the promises we make to God and, ever more, for carrying them out.
Vocation_Job: Priest, Founder of Religious Orders, Educator, Charitable Worker

Name: Saint Louise de Marillac
Historical_Birthplace: Ferrières-en-Brie near Meux, Kingdom of France
Major_Events: Co-founded the Daughters of Charity with St. Vincent de Paul in 1633
Established hospitals, orphanages, and schools across France
Wrote the rule for the Daughters of Charity, which was approved in 1655
Notable_Contributions: Revolutionized the role of women in religious life through active service outside convents
Led humanitarian efforts to care for the sick, poor, and orphaned
Inspired the global expansion of the Daughters of Charity to serve the needy
Quotes: On the day of St. Sebastian, I was in the church at Montmartre when I felt a strong calling to give myself to God so as to do his most holy will for my entire life.
The people of Charity know the happiness of having this relationship with Our Lord, of being with Him wherever they go to help their neighbour.

Name: Saint Elizabeth Ann Seton
Historical_Birthplace: New York City, Province of New York, British America
Modern_Birthplace: New York City, New York, USA
Religious_Order: Sisters of Charity of St. Joseph's
Major_Events: Founded the Sisters of Charity of St. Joseph's in 1809
Established the first free Catholic school for girls in the U.S.
Canonized on September 14, 1975, by Pope Paul VI
Notable_Contributions: Pioneered Catholic education in the United States
Founded the first American congregation of religious sisters
Created foundations for Catholic charitable services in the U.S.
Quotes: If [something] succeeds, I bless God, if it does not succeed … I bless God, because then it will be right that things should not succeed.
O my God! Forgive what I have been, correct what I am, and direct what I shall be.
Let my heart, lost in yours, have no other movement, no other will, no other love, than the will of my divine Master.

Name: Saint John Bosco
Major_Events: Founded the Salesians of Don Bosco in 1859
Established the Oratory of St. Francis de Sales for boys
Published the Salesian Bulletin
Founded the Daughters of Mary Help of Christians with St. Maria Domenica Mazzarello
Notable_Contributions: Developed the Salesian Preventive System of education based on love rather than punishment
Advocated for the rights of apprentices through labor contracts
Provided vocational training and catechetical education for underprivileged youth
Authored numerous religious and educational publications
Quotes: Not with violence, but with words.
Do not put off till tomorrow the good you can do today. You may not have a tomorrow.
Tell my boys that I wait for them all in Paradise.

Name: Saint Maria Goretti
Major_Events: Resisted Alessandro Serenelli's assault, declaring it a sin against God
Forgave her attacker on her deathbed
Appeared in a dream to Alessandro Serenelli, leading to his conversion
Canonized as a saint by Pope Pius XII in 1950
Notable_Contributions: Became a model of purity and forgiveness
Inspired conversions and devotions to chastity and mercy
Patron saint of victims of sexual violence and youth
Quotes: No! It is a sin! God does not want it!
Yes, for the love of Jesus I forgive him... and I want him to be with me in Paradise.

Name: Saint Thérèse of Lisieux
Major_Events: Entered the Carmel of Lisieux at age 15 on 1888-04-09
Made her religious profession on 1890-09-08
Canonized by Pope Pius XI on 1925-05-17
Declared a Doctor of the Church by Pope John Paul II on 1997-10-19
Notable_Contributions: Developed the 'Little Way,' a path of spiritual childhood marked by trust and surrender
Authored 'Story of a Soul,' an influential spiritual autobiography
Promoted a spirituality of simplicity and profound love for God
Quotes: I shall spend my heaven in doing good upon earth.
I prefer the monotony of obscure sacrifice to all ecstasies. To pick up a pin for love can convert a soul.
My God, ‘I choose all!’ I don’t want to be a saint by halves; I’m not afraid to suffer for You.

Name: Saint Bernadette Soubirous
Religious_Order: Sisters of Charity and Christian Instruction of Nevers
Major_Events: Experienced 18 apparitions of the Virgin Mary at Lourdes in 1858
Identified the Virgin Mary as 'The Immaculate Conception'
Directed the building of a chapel at the apparition site
Canonized as a saint on December 8, 1933
Notable_Contributions: Inspired the establishment of the Marian shrine at Lourdes, a major pilgrimage site
Spread devotion to Our Lady of Lourdes
Lived a life of penance and prayer as a religious sister
Quotes: I must die to myself continually and accept trials without complaining.
Blessed Mary, Mother of God, pray for me. A poor sinner, a poor sinner.
All this is good for Heaven!

Name: Saint Joan of Arc
Historical_Birthplace: Domrémy, Duchy of Bar, Kingdom of France
Historical_Death_Place: Rouen, Duchy of Normandy, Kingdom of France
Major_Events: Led French forces to victory at the Siege of Orléans in 1429
Enabled the coronation of Charles VII in Reims
Captured by Burgundian forces in 1430 and sold to the English
Tried and executed for heresy in 1431
Notable_Contributions: Restored French morale during the Hundred Years' War
Symbolized national unity and faith in France
Canonized as a saint in 1920
Quotes: I am not afraid; I was born to do this.
If I am not, may God put me there; and if I am, may God so keep me.
In God's name! Let us go on bravely!
My words and deeds are all in God’s Hands: in all, I wait upon Him.

Name: Saint Anthony of Padua
Virtues_Traits: Devotion to the poor and needy
Major_Events: Joined the Canons Regular of St. Augustine in 1210
Entered the Franciscan Order in 1220
Preached across Italy and southern France against heresies
Taught theology in Bologna and Montpellier
Proclaimed a Doctor of the Church by Pope Pius XII in 1946
Notable_Contributions: Renowned preacher and teacher of theology
Advocated for the poor and social justice
Known as the 'Wonder-worker' for miracles attributed to him
Writings include sermons for Sundays and feast days
Established Franciscan communities in Italy
Quotes: Actions speak louder than words; let your words teach and your actions speak.
Attribute to God every good that you have received. If you take credit for something that does not belong to you, you are committing theft.

Name: Saint Pio of Pietrelcina
Major_Events: Received the stigmata in 1918, which remained until his death
Founded the Casa Sollievo della Sofferenza in 1956
Canonized by Pope John Paul II on 16 June 2002
Notable_Contributions: Devoted his life to prayer and the sacraments
Built the House for the Relief of Suffering
Provided spiritual direction and heard confessions for countless individuals
Quotes: Pray, hope and don’t worry. Worry is useless. Our Merciful Lord will listen to your prayer.
Prayer is the best weapon we possess, the key that opens the heart of God.
Today’s society does not pray. That is why it is falling apart.

Name: Saint Maximilian Kolbe
Historical_Birthplace: Zduńska Wola, Congress Poland, Russian Empire
Major_Events: Founded the Militia Immaculatae in 1917
Established Niepokalanów (City of the Immaculata) in Poland as a major evangelization center
Published devotional and anti-Nazi literature
Arrested by the Gestapo in 1941 and sent to Auschwitz
Volunteered to die in place of a fellow prisoner, Franciszek Gajowniczek
Notable_Contributions: Promoted devotion to the Virgin Mary
Advanced Marian theology, including insights on the Immaculate Conception
Used modern media for evangelization, including radio and publishing
Symbolized self-sacrifice and Christian love through his martyrdom
Quotes: I am a Catholic priest. I would like to take his place, because he has a wife and children.
Grant that I might praise Thee, O Most Holy Virgin. Grant that I might praise Thee with my effort and my personal sacrifice.

Name: Saint Edith Stein
Major_Events: Converted to Catholicism on 1922-01-01 after reading the works of St. Teresa of Ávila
Entered the Discalced Carmelite convent in Cologne in 1934, taking the name Teresa Benedicta of the Cross
Wrote significant philosophical and theological works, including 'Finite and Eternal Being' and 'The Science of the Cross'
Arrested by the Gestapo on 1942-08-02 and deported to Auschwitz
Martyred in Auschwitz gas chambers on 1942-08-09
Notable_Contributions: Influenced Catholic philosophy by combining phenomenology with Thomism
Translated significant works of St. Thomas Aquinas
Wrote extensively on empathy, the human soul, and spiritual theology
Served as a symbol of solidarity with the Jewish people during the Holocaust
Quotes: The human person is not just something, but someone. Not just an object to be used, but a subject to be respected and loved.
Our neighbor's spiritual need transcends every commandment. Everything else we do is a means to an end. But love is an end already, since God is love.
To be a Christian means to forgive the inexcusable because God has forgiven the inexcusable in you.

Name: Saint Kateri Tekakwitha
Historical_Death_Place: St. Francis Xavier Mission at Sault St. Louis, New France
Major_Events: Baptized at age 20 on Easter Sunday, 1676
Took a vow of perpetual virginity on March 25, 1679
Canonized on October 21, 2012, by Pope Benedict XVI
Notable_Contributions: First Native American canonized by the Catholic Church
Demonstrated exemplary devotion and penance
Inspired conversions among her people
Quotes: I have consecrated myself entirely to Jesus, the Son of Mary, and He alone I have chosen as a husband, and He alone will take me for a wife.
Who can tell me what is most pleasing to God that I may do it?

Name: Saint Damien of Molokai
Historical_Birthplace: Tremelo, Province of Brabant, Kingdom of Belgium
Religious_Order: Congregation of the Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary (SS.CC.)
Major_Events: Volunteered to serve in the leper colony of Molokai in 1873
Built homes, hospitals, and churches for the leper community
Contracted leprosy in 1884 while serving the colony
Buried under the Pandanus tree where he first slept in Molokai
Notable_Contributions: Improved living conditions for lepers in Molokai
Advocated for leprosy patients' dignity and rights
Spread awareness about the plight of leprosy patients worldwide
Quotes: I make myself a leper with the lepers to gain all to Jesus Christ.
It is at the foot of the altar that we find the strength we need in our isolation.
Without the constant presence of our Divine Master, I would never be able to cast my lot with that of the lepers.

Name: Saint Mother Teresa of Calcutta
Major_Events: Founded the Missionaries of Charity in 1950
Received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979
Canonized as a saint on September 4, 2016
Established numerous homes for the dying, AIDS patients, lepers, and orphans
Notable_Contributions: Devoted life to serving the poorest of the poor
Expanded the Missionaries of Charity to over 130 countries
Raised global awareness for the dignity of the poor and marginalized
Inspired worldwide humanitarian work
Quotes: I have found the paradox that if I love until it hurts, then there is no hurt, but only more love.

At the end of our lives, we will not be judged by how many diplomas we have received, how much money we have made, or how many great things we have done. We will be judged by, 'I was hungry and you gave me to eat. I was naked and you clothed me. I was homeless and you took me in.'

Name: Saint Faustina Kowalska
Historical_Birthplace: Głogowiec, Łęczyca County, Congress Poland, Russian Empire
Religious_Order: Congregation of the Sisters of Our Lady of Mercy
Major_Events: Received frequent visions of Jesus Christ and recorded them in her diary
Commissioned the first Divine Mercy image based on her vision of Jesus
Promoted the Divine Mercy devotion which included the chaplet, novena, and Divine Mercy Sunday
Canonized on April 30, 2000, by Pope John Paul II
Notable_Contributions: Inspired the worldwide spread of the Divine Mercy devotion
Authored 'The Diary of Saint Maria Faustina Kowalska: Divine Mercy in My Soul'
Established the Divine Mercy chaplet and novena as key spiritual practices
Quotes: Humility, humility, and ever humility, as we can do nothing of ourselves; all is purely and simply God's grace.
Jesus, I trust in You.
I desire to reflect Your compassionate heart, full of mercy; I want to glorify it.

Name: Saint John Paul II
Major_Events: Elected the first non-Italian pope in 455 years on October 16, 1978
Survived an assassination attempt on May 13, 1981
Played a pivotal role in the fall of Communism in Eastern Europe
Established World Youth Day
Canonized 483 saints and beatified 1,344 people
Notable_Contributions: Promoted interfaith dialogue with Judaism, Islam, and other Christian denominations
Contributed to the peaceful removal of Communism in Eastern Europe
Published the Catechism of the Catholic Church in 1992
Traveled to 129 countries, becoming one of the most-traveled popes in history
Advocated for human rights and dignity globally
Quotes: Do not be afraid! Open wide the doors for Christ…. Christ knows ‘what is in man.’ He alone knows it.
In everything that happened to me on that day, I felt (the Mother of God’s) extraordinary motherly protection and care, which turned out to be stronger than the deadly bullet.

Name: Saint Gregory of Nazianzus
Major_Events: Composed the Five Theological Orations defending the Holy Trinity
Oversaw the Second Ecumenical Council (Constantinople, 381)
Became Archbishop of Constantinople in 380
Reconciled divisions caused by Arianism
Notable_Contributions: Promoted Nicene Orthodoxy against Arianism
Authored theological works foundational to Trinitarian doctrine
Prolific poet and writer on Christian theology
Quotes: Let me be as the Prophet Jonah! I was responsible for the storm, but I would sacrifice myself for the salvation of the ship. Seize me and throw me... I was not happy when I ascended the throne, and gladly would I descend it.
Vocation_Job: Theologian, Bishop, Poet, Archbishop of Constantinople

Name: Saint Basil the Great
Major_Events: Ordained as deacon in 362 by Bishop Meletius of Antioch
Became Bishop of Caesarea in 370
Founded the Basiliad, a charitable complex for the poor and sick
Defended the Nicene Creed against Arianism
Notable_Contributions: Pioneered cenobitic monasticism in the East
Writings on theology, including 'On the Holy Spirit' and 'Against Eunomius'
Contributions to Christian liturgy and communal monastic rules
Advocated for and practiced social justice and charity
Quotes: A tree is known by its fruit; a man by his deeds.
When someone steals another’s clothes, we call them a thief. Should we not give the same name to one who could clothe the naked and does not?

Name: Saint Athanasius of Alexandria
Major_Events: Participated in the First Council of Nicaea (325)
Elected Patriarch of Alexandria (328)
Exiled five times by four Roman emperors
Defended the Nicene Creed against Arianism
Notable_Contributions: Wrote 'De Incarnatione' establishing the divinity of Christ
Promoted early monasticism through his biography of St. Anthony
Defended Trinitarian theology against Arianism
Quotes: Let what was confessed by the Fathers of Nicaea prevail.

Name: Saint Cyril of Alexandria
Historical_Birthplace: Theodosius, Province of Egypt, Roman Empire
Historical_Death_Place: Alexandria, Province of Egypt, Byzantine Empire
Major_Events: Succeeded his uncle Theophilus as Patriarch of Alexandria in 412
Expelled Jews from Alexandria after violent conflicts
Closed Novatian heretical churches
Presided over the Council of Ephesus in 431, which condemned Nestorianism
Composed the Twelve Anathemas against Nestorian heresy
Notable_Contributions: Defended the doctrine of Theotokos (Mary as Mother of God)
Clarified the hypostatic union of Christ’s divine and human natures
Wrote extensive theological treatises and commentaries
Synthesized teachings of earlier Church Fathers
Declared Doctor of the Church in 1882
Quotes: We proclaim the holy Virgin to be the Mother of God because God the Word was incarnate and became man.

Name: Saint John Chrysostom
Historical_Death_Place: Comana, Diocese of Pontus, Eastern Roman Empire
Major_Events: Ordained a deacon in 381
Ordained a priest in 386 at Antioch
Became Archbishop of Constantinople in 398
Exiled in 403 due to conflicts with imperial authorities
Died en route to exile in 407
Notable_Contributions: Extensive homilies on Scripture
Development of the Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom
Writings on pastoral theology
Defense of the poor and criticism of wealth misuse
Quotes: The Church is the house of the heavenly Father, one Body and one Spirit.
To tear asunder the Church means nothing less than to fall into heresy.

Name: Saint Hilary of Poitiers
Major_Events: Converted to Christianity from Neoplatonism
Elected Bishop of Poitiers
Exiled to Phrygia for opposing Arianism
Wrote De Trinitate to defend the doctrine of the Trinity
Proclaimed Doctor of the Church in 1851
Notable_Contributions: Authored De Trinitate, a foundational work on the doctrine of the Trinity
Composed some of the earliest Christian hymns in the West
Strengthened orthodoxy against Arianism in Gaul
Wrote a commentary on the Psalms and the Gospel of Matthew
Quotes: For one to attempt to speak of God in terms more precise than he himself has used: -- to undertake such a thing is to embark upon the boundless, to dare the incomprehensible.

Name: Saint Ephrem the Syrian
Major_Events: Assisted in founding the School of Nisibis
Expelled from Nisibis after its fall to the Persians in 363
Founded a theological school in Edessa
Declared a Doctor of the Church in 1920 by Pope Benedict XV
Notable_Contributions: Composed over 400 hymns and 3,000 poems
Defended Nicene orthodoxy through hymns and writings
Promoted catechesis and liturgical devotion through theological poetry
Quotes: I have chanced upon weeds, my brothers, that wear the color of wheat, to choke the good seed.
The soul is your bride, the body is your bridal chamber.
He has saved us without wall, and taught us that He is our wall.

Name: Saint Polycarp of Smyrna
Major_Events: Taught directly by the Apostle John
Appointed Bishop of Smyrna by the Apostles
Fought heresies such as Gnosticism
Met with Pope Anicetus to discuss the date of Easter
Martyred by burning and stabbing for refusing to renounce Christ
Notable_Contributions: Preserved Apostolic teachings
Wrote the Letter to the Philippians
Served as a critical link between the Apostolic and Patristic ages
Quotes: I have served Him for eighty-six years, and He has done me no harm. How could I curse my King who saved me?
You threaten me with fire, which burns for an hour, and after a little is extinguished. But you are ignorant of the fire of the coming judgment and of eternal punishment, reserved for the ungodly.

Name: Saint Ignatius of Antioch
Major_Events: Became the third Bishop of Antioch around 69 AD
Wrote seven influential letters to Christian communities during his journey to Rome
Martyred by being thrown to wild beasts in the Colosseum
Notable_Contributions: Introduced the term 'Catholic Church' to describe the universal body of believers
Encouraged unity and apostolic tradition in his letters
Defended the Eucharist and the real presence of Christ
Quotes: I am God’s wheat, and I am to be ground by the teeth of wild beasts, so that I may become the pure bread of Christ.
Permit me to be an imitator of the passion of my God.
I thank you, O Lord, that You have vouchsafed to honour me with a perfect love towards You, and have made me to be bound with iron chains, like Your Apostle Paul.

Name: Saint Justin Martyr
Major_Events: Converted to Christianity after studying various philosophies
Wrote the 'First Apology' and 'Second Apology' defending Christianity
Martyred for refusing to sacrifice to Roman gods
Notable_Contributions: Defended Christianity using Greek philosophy
Provided early descriptions of Christian liturgical practices
Laid groundwork for Christian theology engaging Greek philosophy
Quotes: No one in his right mind gives up piety for impiety.

We hope to suffer torment for the sake of our Lord Jesus Christ and so be saved. For this will bring us salvation and confidence as we stand before the more terrible and universal judgment-seat of our Lord and Savior.

When I was a disciple of Plato, hearing the accusations made against the Christians and seeing them intrepid in the face of death and of all that men fear, I said to myself that it was impossible that they should be living in evil and in the love of pleasure.

Name: Saint Perpetua
Major_Events: Converted to Christianity despite Roman persecution
Imprisoned and martyred in Carthage
Wrote 'The Passion of Saints Perpetua and Felicity', a powerful first-person account of her trial and visions
Notable_Contributions: Provided one of the earliest known Christian writings by a woman
Inspired early Christian communities through her martyrdom
Her story was read in liturgies for centuries
Quotes: Neither can I call myself by any other name than what I am—a Christian.
Stand fast in the faith, and love one another. Do not let our sufferings be a stumbling block to you.

Name: Saint Felicity
Major_Events: Imprisoned for her Christian faith while pregnant
Gave birth to her child in prison shortly before her execution
Martyred alongside Saint Perpetua and others in the amphitheater
Notable_Contributions: Served as an inspiration for early Christians through her steadfast faith
Encouraged Christians to remain strong in their beliefs despite persecution
Quotes: Another will be within me, who will suffer on my behalf, seeing that it is for Him that I am to suffer.

Name: Saint Cecilia
Major_Events: Converted her husband Valerian and his brother Tiburtius to Christianity
Facilitated the baptism of over 400 people by Pope Urban I
Survived attempted suffocation in a heated bath
Fatally wounded but lived for three days while preaching and praying
Notable_Contributions: Inspired the early Christian community through her martyrdom and evangelization
Donated her home to be used as a church
Regarded as the patroness of music due to her spiritual devotion expressed through song

Name: Saint Lucy of Syracuse
Major_Events: Consecrated her virginity to God and refused marriage
Cured her mother's hemorrhagic illness through faith and intercession of Saint Agatha
Denounced as a Christian by her suitor and persecuted under Diocletian's reign
Miraculously resisted attempts to defile and harm her, including being immovable by oxen and unharmed by fire
Executed by sword after prolonged torture, including having her eyes gouged out
Notable_Contributions: Advocated for the poor by distributing her wealth
Inspired devotion and veneration as a model of faith and light during persecution
Became a symbol of light and hope, celebrated widely in Europe, especially in Scandinavian traditions
Quotes: Whatever you give away at death for the Lord’s sake you give because you cannot take it with you. Give now to the true Savior, while you are healthy, whatever you intended to give away at your death.

I am a servant of the Eternal God and He said: ‘When you are led to the kings and princes do not give thought how or what you have to say because you will not be talking yourself but the Holy Spirit is speaking in you.’
The chaste are the temple of God, and the Holy Spirit dwells in them.

Name: Saint Agnes of Rome
Major_Events: Refused marriage proposals to remain consecrated to Christ
Condemned to death after refusing to renounce her faith
Miraculously saved from fire before being executed by beheading
Notable_Contributions: Inspired devotion to chastity and faith
Served as a model of unwavering faith during Christian persecutions
Quotes: Jesus Christ is my only Spouse.
I am already promised to the Lord of the Universe. He is more splendid than the sun and the stars, and He has said He will never leave me!
I would offend my Spouse if I were to try to please you. He chose me first and He shall have me!

Name: Saint Agatha of Sicily
Major_Events: Refused marriage proposals and vowed virginity
Arrested during Emperor Decius' persecution of Christians
Tortured, including having her breasts cut off, for her refusal to renounce her faith
Miraculously healed by a vision of Saint Peter while in prison
Died after being subjected to severe torture, including being rolled over hot coals and sharp shards
Notable_Contributions: Became a symbol of courage and purity in the face of persecution
Intercessor for those suffering from breast cancer
Invoked for protection against volcanic eruptions and fires
Patroness of nurses and rape victims
Quotes: Jesus Christ, Lord of all, you see my heart, you know my desires. Possess all that I am. I am your sheep: make me worthy to overcome the devil.
Lord, my Creator, you have always protected me from the cradle; you have taken me from the love of the world and given me the patience to suffer. Receive my soul.

Name: Saint Monica
Historical_Birthplace: Tagaste, Numidia Cirtensis, Western Roman Empire
Major_Events: Converted her pagan husband, Patricius, and her mother-in-law to Christianity
Persistently prayed and worked for the conversion of her son, Augustine
Witnessed Saint Augustine's baptism by Saint Ambrose in 387
Traveled extensively to accompany Augustine, including to Milan and Rome
Notable_Contributions: Her prayers and perseverance led to the conversion of Saint Augustine, one of the most influential theologians in Christianity
Left a legacy of faith, patience, and devotion as a model for mothers and Christians
Quotes: "Lay this body anywhere, let not care for it trouble you; this only I ask you, that you remember me at the altar of the Lord, wherever you be."

Name: Saint Helena
Major_Events: Discovery of the True Cross in Jerusalem
Erection of the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem
Erection of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem
Influence on Constantine's Christianization of the Roman Empire
Notable_Contributions: Promoted Christianity throughout the Roman Empire
Built significant churches at Christian holy sites
Preserved and honored sacred Christian relics and locations

Name: Saint Bridget of Sweden
Religious_Order: Order of the Most Holy Savior (Bridgettines)
Major_Events: Founded the Order of the Most Holy Savior (Bridgettines) in 1346
Made a pilgrimage to Santiago de Compostela with her husband
Actively advocated for the pope’s return to Rome during the Avignon Papacy
Visited the Holy Land in 1372
Notable_Contributions: Established the Bridgettine double monastery in Vadstena, Sweden
Produced influential mystical writings and revelations
Promoted care for the sick, poor, and marginalized
Quotes: "True wisdom, then, consists in works, not in great talents, which the world admires; for the wise in the world's estimation . . . are the foolish who set at naught the will of God, and know not how to control their passions."
"In accordance with his surname, Thaddeus, the amiable or loving, he will show himself most willing to give help."
"Woman, hear me; I am your God, who wishes to speak with you. Fear not, for I am the Creator of all, and not a deceiver."
Vocation_Job: Mystic, Founder of Religious Order, Advocate for Social Justice

Name: Saint Rose of Lima
Historical_Birthplace: Lima, Viceroyalty of Peru, Spanish Empire
Historical_Death_Place: Lima, Viceroyalty of Peru, Spanish Empire
Major_Events: Joined Third Order of Saint Dominic at age 20
Dedicated her life to prayer and care for the poor
Built a small grotto for prayer and penance
Established a home-based infirmary for the sick and poor
Notable_Contributions: First saint canonized from the Americas
Founder of social work in Peru
Symbol of devotion and virtue in Latin America
Quotes: Lord, increase my sufferings, and with them increase your love in my heart.

Name: Saint Martin de Porres
Historical_Birthplace: Lima, Viceroyalty of Peru, Spanish Empire
Historical_Death_Place: Lima, Viceroyalty of Peru, Spanish Empire
Major_Events: Accepted as a Dominican lay brother in 1603 despite racial prejudice
Worked tirelessly in the monastery infirmary caring for the sick
Founded an orphanage and hospital for abandoned children and slaves
Performed numerous miraculous acts including healing, bilocation, and levitation
Notable_Contributions: Cared for the sick and marginalized regardless of race or status
Established a school for poor youth in Lima
Distributed food and alms to the poor daily
Promoted racial harmony and social justice
Quotes: Everything, even sweeping, scraping vegetables, weeding a garden and waiting on the sick could be a prayer, if it were offered to God.
Do not complain, that shows discontent with the will of God in the present moment. That is also proof of impatience.
Always consider others as more holy and more worthy than you, at the same time strive to be as holy as you can be.

Name: Saint Philip Neri
Major_Events: Founded the Congregation of the Oratory in 1575
Organized the Seven Churches Walk pilgrimage
Promoted spiritual renewal during the Counter-Reformation
Notable_Contributions: Reformed spirituality in Rome during the Counter-Reformation
Established a new model of communal priestly life
Integrated joy, music, and humor into spiritual practices
Quotes: Let me get through today, and I shall not fear tomorrow.
Last of all, we must die.
Vocation_Job: Priest, Founder of the Oratory, Mystic

Name: Saint Charles Borromeo
Historical_Birthplace: Castle of Arona, Duchy of Milan
Major_Events: Played a key role in the Council of Trent (1545-1564)
Became Archbishop of Milan in 1564
Established seminaries and the Confraternity of Christian Doctrine (CCD)
Survived an assassination attempt by the Humiliati order
Led relief efforts during the famine of 1570 and plague of 1576
Notable_Contributions: Reformed the Archdiocese of Milan, addressing corruption and laxity among clergy
Helped implement the Tridentine Reforms
Founded Sunday schools and advanced religious education
Acted as a spiritual mentor to St. Aloysius Gonzaga
Quotes: Wherever there is sufficient number of clerics, it would be well to chant the psalms and litanies with some intelligible and devout music to arouse greater devotion among the people.
Vocation_Job: Cardinal, Archbishop of Milan, Theologian, Educator

Name: Saint Robert Bellarmine
Major_Events: Appointed first Jesuit professor of theology at Louvain in 1570
Wrote 'Disputations on the Controversies', a defense of Catholic theology during the Counter-Reformation
Named a cardinal by Pope Clement VIII in 1599
Became Archbishop of Capua in 1602
Canonized by Pope Pius XI in 1930
Declared Doctor of the Church in 1931
Notable_Contributions: Authored catechisms translated into 62 languages
Defended Catholic doctrine against Protestant Reformers
Played a significant role in implementing the reforms of the Council of Trent
Published works on spirituality and theology, including 'The Art of Dying Well'
Quotes: The school of Christ is the school of love. In the last day, when the general examination takes place … Love will be the whole syllabus.
Charity is that with which no man is lost, and without which no man is saved.
The walls won’t catch cold.
Vocation_Job: Jesuit priest, theologian, cardinal, archbishop, author

Name: Saint Alphonsus Liguori
Religious_Order: Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer (Redemptorists)
Major_Events: Founded the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer in 1732
Appointed Bishop of Sant'Agata de' Goti in 1762
Resigned as Bishop in 1775 due to ill health
Declared a Doctor of the Church in 1871
Notable_Contributions: Authored influential works on moral theology, such as 'Moral Theology' and 'Glories of Mary'
Founded the 'Evening Chapels' for prayer and catechesis among the poor
Reformed seminaries and clergy in his diocese
Promoted devotion to the Blessed Sacrament and the Virgin Mary
Quotes: The heart of man is, so to speak, the paradise of God. Oh, love the God who loves you! Since His delights are to be with you, let yours be found in Him.
I have never preached a sermon which the poorest old woman in the congregation could not understand.
Scruples are useful in the beginning of conversion... they cleanse the soul, and at the same time make it careful.
Vocation_Job: Priest, Bishop, Theologian, Founder of a Religious Order

Name: Saint Peter Claver
Major_Events: Ordained a Jesuit priest in 1616 in Cartagena
Dedicated 38 years to ministering to enslaved Africans in Cartagena
Baptized over 300,000 enslaved people
Advocated for better treatment of enslaved individuals and chastised oppressors
Canonized by Pope Leo XIII in 1888
Notable_Contributions: Ministered to the physical, emotional, and spiritual needs of enslaved Africans
Provided food, medicine, and catechesis aboard slave ships and plantations
Promoted the dignity of enslaved individuals despite societal norms
Established himself as a model of Christian charity and racial justice
Quotes: We must speak to them with our hands before we speak to them with our lips.

Name: Saint John Vianney
Major_Events: Ordained a priest in 1815
Appointed Curé of Ars in 1818
Established La Providence, an orphanage for girls
Canonized by Pope Pius XI in 1925
Named Patron Saint of Parish Priests by Pope Pius XI in 1929
Notable_Contributions: Revived the faith of the community in Ars through prayer, penance, and preaching
Spent up to 16 hours a day hearing confessions
Converted countless sinners through his ministry
Became a model of priestly holiness and pastoral care
Quotes: If we really understood the priest on earth, we would die: not of fear, but of love.
The priesthood is the love of the heart of Jesus.
I give sinners a small penance, and the rest I do in their place.

Name: Saint Catherine Labouré
Major_Events: Received apparitions of the Virgin Mary in 1830
Entrusted with the mission of creating the Miraculous Medal
Witnessed the rapid spread of the Miraculous Medal devotion
Served 46 years at the Enghien Hospice caring for the elderly and infirmed
Notable_Contributions: Popularized devotion to the Miraculous Medal
Inspired global Marian devotion
Provided a model of quiet and faithful service
Contributed to the spread of the Vincentian charism
Quotes: Now, dear Blessed Mother, now you will be my Mother.
I knew nothing. I was nothing. For this reason God picked me out.
You must give everything to God. Remember, you are leaving God for God.

Name: Saint Margaret Mary Alacoque
Patron_Of: Devotees of the Sacred Heart of Jesus
Major_Events: Promoted devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus
Received visions of Christ instructing her in the devotion
Inspired the institution of the Feast of the Sacred Heart
Notable_Contributions: Established devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus
Promoted the First Fridays devotion and Holy Hour
Encouraged reparation for sins to the Sacred Heart
Quotes: What have I in heaven, and what do I desire on earth, but Thee alone, O my God?
This divine Heart is a throne of flames, more brilliant than the sun and transparent as crystal.
Vocation_Job: Nun, Mystic, Apostle of the Sacred Heart

Name: Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini
Historical_Birthplace: Sant'Angelo Lodigiano, Kingdom of Lombardy–Venetia, Austrian Empire
Religious_Order: Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart of Jesus
Major_Events: Founded the Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart of Jesus in 1880
Naturalized as a U.S. citizen in 1909
Founded 67 institutions including schools, hospitals, and orphanages across the United States, Latin America, and Europe
Canonized as the first U.S. citizen saint in 1946 by Pope Pius XII
Notable_Contributions: Advocated for and supported Italian immigrants in the United States
Established institutions providing care for the poor, sick, and uneducated
Inspired others to serve in the healthcare and educational fields
Quotes: Not to the East, but to the West.

Name: Saint Gianna Beretta Molla
Major_Events: Earned degrees in medicine and surgery in 1949
Specialized in pediatrics in 1952
Founded a medical clinic in Mesero, Italy
Married Pietro Molla in 1955
Sacrificed her life to save her unborn child in 1962
Notable_Contributions: Devoted her life to her family, patients, and faith
Lived as a model of Christian motherhood and medical professionalism
Canonized as a modern saint in 2004
Quotes: If you must decide between me and the child, do not hesitate: choose the child—I insist on it.
Love is the most beautiful sentiment that the Lord has put into the soul of men and women.

Name: Saint André Bessette
Historical_Death_Place: Saint-Laurent, Montreal Region, Dominion of Canada
Major_Events: Entered the Congregation of Holy Cross on December 27, 1870
Professed final vows on February 2, 1874
Opened Saint Joseph’s Oratory in 1904
Canonized by Pope Benedict XVI on October 17, 2010
Notable_Contributions: Promoted devotion to Saint Joseph
Built Saint Joseph’s Oratory in Montreal, a major pilgrimage site
Attributed with thousands of miraculous healings
Quotes: Saint Joseph will never let you down. He’s the reason you are healed. Continue praying to his foster Son, Jesus, and Mother Mary.

Name: Saint Oscar Romero
Major_Events: Ordained as a priest in 1942
Appointed Archbishop of San Salvador in 1977
Became an outspoken advocate for the poor and victims of violence
Assassinated while celebrating Mass in 1980
Notable_Contributions: Utilized homilies to denounce human rights abuses and promote justice
Symbolized the Church's preferential option for the poor
Inspired global awareness about El Salvador's oppression
Canonized as a saint by Pope Francis in 2018
Quotes: Aspire not to have more, but to be more.
If I am killed, I shall arise in the Salvadoran people.
In the name of God, stop the repression!
Vocation_Job: Priest, Archbishop, Advocate for social justice

Name: Saint Ignatius of Loyola
Birth_Name: Íñigo López de Oñaz y Loyola
Historical_Birthplace: Castle Loyola, Guipúzcoa Province, Crown of Castile
Patron_Of: Basque provinces of Gipuzkoa and Biscay
Major_Events: Wounded at the Battle of Pamplona in 1521, prompting a spiritual transformation
Developed the Spiritual Exercises during his time in Manresa
Founded the Society of Jesus in 1540 with papal approval
Elected the first Superior General of the Jesuits in 1541
Canonized as a saint in 1622
Notable_Contributions: Founder of the Jesuit religious order
Authored the Spiritual Exercises, a foundational guide for spiritual retreats
Promoted education and intellectual rigor as tools for faith and reform
Contributed to the Counter-Reformation through missionary work and education
Quotes: Man was created to praise, reverence, and serve God our Lord, and by this means to save his soul.
Vocation_Job: Priest, Theologian, Founder of the Jesuits

Name: Saint Thomas More
Major_Events: Served as Lord Chancellor of England (1529-1532)
Authored 'Utopia' in 1516
Refused to accept King Henry VIII as Supreme Head of the Church of England
Executed for treason after refusing the Oath of Supremacy
Notable_Contributions: Authored 'Utopia', a foundational work in political philosophy
Defended the primacy of the Pope over the Church
Embodied the value of moral conscience in public service
Quotes: The king's good servant, but God's first.

Name: Saint Teresa of Calcutta
Major_Events: Received the 'call within a call' in 1946 to serve the poorest of the poor
Founded the Missionaries of Charity in 1950
Received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979
Canonized as Saint Teresa of Calcutta in 2016
Notable_Contributions: Established homes for the dying, orphanages, and leprosy treatment centers
Expanded Missionaries of Charity to over 123 countries
Advocated for the dignity and care of the poorest
Quotes: I have found the paradox that if I love until it hurts, then there is no hurt, but only more love.

At the end of our lives, we will not be judged by how many diplomas we have received, how much money we have made, or how many great things we have done. We will be judged by, 'I was hungry and you gave me to eat. I was naked and you clothed me. I was homeless and you took me in.'
Vocation_Job: Nun, Missionary, Founder of Missionaries of Charity

Name: Saint John Chrysostom
Major_Events: Ordained a deacon in 381 and a priest in 386
Appointed Archbishop of Constantinople in 398
Exiled twice due to conflicts with Empress Eudoxia and ecclesiastical authorities
Introduced liturgical reforms and supported missions to surrounding regions
Declared Doctor of the Church for his contributions to Christian teaching
Notable_Contributions: Authored over 700 sermons and numerous letters
Composed the 'Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom,' central to Eastern Orthodox worship
Wrote theological treatises and commentaries on Scripture
Advocated for the poor, criticized corruption, and preached against the abuse of wealth
Promoted unity within the Church and resisted heresies
Quotes: The Church is the house of the heavenly Father, one Body and one Spirit.
If you cannot find Christ in the beggar at the church door, you will not find Him in the chalice.
Prayer is the light of the soul, true knowledge of God.

Name: Saint Josephine Bakhita
Major_Events: Kidnapped and sold into slavery at the age of nine
Baptized and confirmed in 1890 in Venice, Italy
Declared free by Italian courts in 1885
Joined the Canossian Daughters of Charity in 1893 and took final vows in 1896
Canonized by Pope John Paul II on October 1, 2000
Notable_Contributions: Advocated for human dignity and freedom
Served her community through humble acts such as cooking, sewing, and welcoming visitors
Became a symbol of hope and forgiveness for victims of human trafficking
Quotes: Be good, love the Lord, pray for those who do not know Him. What a great grace it is to know God!

If I were to meet the slave traders who kidnapped me and even those who tortured me, I would kneel and kiss their hands, for if these things had not happened, I would not have been a Christian and a religious today.

Name: Saint Louis IX
Major_Events: Crowned King of France at age 12 under regency of his mother Blanche of Castile
Led the Seventh Crusade (1248-1250) and Eighth Crusade (1270)
Established the Parlement of Paris
Commissioned Sainte-Chapelle as a reliquary for the Crown of Thorns
Canonized in 1297 by Pope Boniface VIII
Notable_Contributions: Reformed the French legal system by abolishing trials by ordeal and promoting the presumption of innocence
Established hospitals and homes for the poor
Promoted higher education including founding the Sorbonne
Acted as an international mediator during disputes across Europe
Quotes: The peace and blessings of the realm come to us through the poor.

Name: Saint Helen
Major_Events: Discovered the True Cross during a pilgrimage to the Holy Land
Supervised the demolition of pagan temples and the construction of Christian churches in Jerusalem, Bethlehem, and Mount of Olives
Contributed to the spread of Christianity throughout the Roman Empire
Notable_Contributions: Promoted Christianity's establishment in the Roman Empire
Preserved and identified sacred Christian relics such as the True Cross
Supported the construction of churches at key Christian sites

Name: Saint Andrew Kim Taegon
Modern_Birthplace: Solmoe, South Chungcheong Province, South Korea
Modern_Death_Place: Saenamteo Martyrs' Shrine, Yongsan District, Seoul, South Korea
Major_Events: Baptized at age 15
Studied in Macau and the Philippines
Ordained as the first Korean-born Catholic priest in Shanghai in 1844
Evangelized in Korea under severe persecution
Arrested, tortured, and martyred by beheading in 1846
Notable_Contributions: First Korean-born Catholic priest
Evangelized and strengthened the Catholic faith in Korea during a time of persecution
Inspired countless Korean Catholics through his martyrdom
Quotes: We have received baptism, entrance into the Church, and the honor of being called Christians. Yet what good will this do us if we are Christians in name only and not in fact?

This is my last hour of life, listen to me attentively: if I have held communication with foreigners, it has been for my religion and my God. It is for Him that I die. My immortal life is on the point of beginning. Become Christians if you wish to be happy after death, because God has eternal chastisements in store for those who have refused to know Him.

Name: Saint Faustina Kowalska
Religious_Order: Congregation of the Sisters of Our Lady of Mercy
Major_Events: Received visions and messages from Jesus about Divine Mercy
Commissioned the first Divine Mercy image with guidance from Father Michał Sopoćko
Kept a diary documenting her mystical experiences, later published as 'The Diary of Saint Maria Faustina Kowalska: Divine Mercy in My Soul'
Instituted devotion to the Divine Mercy Chaplet and Divine Mercy Sunday
Inspired the establishment of the Sisters of Merciful Jesus
Notable_Contributions: Promoted the devotion to Divine Mercy
Wrote extensively about her mystical experiences and teachings of Jesus on mercy
Helped establish the Feast of Divine Mercy Sunday through her revelations
Quotes: Humility, humility, and ever humility, as we can do nothing of ourselves; all is purely and simply God's grace.
Jesus, I trust in You.
I do not want to punish aching mankind, but I desire to heal it, pressing it to my merciful heart.
Neither graces, nor revelations, nor raptures, nor gifts granted to a soul make it perfect, but rather the intimate union of the soul with God.

Name: Saint John of God
Religious_Order: Brothers Hospitallers of Saint John of God
Major_Events: Established a hospital to care for the sick and poor in Granada
Founded the Brothers Hospitallers, a religious order dedicated to serving the sick
Rescued patients from a burning hospital without being harmed by the flames
Notable_Contributions: Founded the Brothers Hospitallers of Saint John of God, now a worldwide religious order
Cared for the sick, poor, and mentally ill
Inspired others to join in service through his example of selfless charity
Quotes: For just as water extinguishes a fire, just so does charity blot out our sins.
There are three things that make me uneasy: The first is that I have received so many graces from God, and have not recognized them, and have repaid them with so little of my own.
The second is that after I am dead, I fear lest the poor women I have rescued, and the poor sinners I have reclaimed, may be treated badly.
The third is that those who have trusted me with money, and whom I have not fully repaid, may suffer loss on my account.
Vocation_Job: Founder of a Religious Order, Caregiver for the Sick and Poor

Name: Saint Benedict the Moor
Religious_Order: Franciscan Order (Order of Friars Minor, Observants)
Major_Events: Freed by his master's promise before his birth
Joined a Franciscan hermit community and became its leader
Transitioned to Franciscan Order after Pope Pius IV disbanded solitary communities
Appointed superior of the Friary of St. Mary in Palermo
Known for miracles, healing, and spiritual guidance
Notable_Contributions: Became a symbol of racial equality and humility
Known for miraculous healing and acts of charity
Inspired devotion to African missions and African American communities
Quotes: Unknown
Vocation_Job: Franciscan lay brother, Cook, Novice master, Spiritual guide

Name: Saint Hildegard of Bingen
Historical_Birthplace: Böckelheim, County Palatine of the Rhine, Holy Roman Empire
Historical_Death_Place: Rupertsberg, County Palatine of the Rhine, Holy Roman Empire
Major_Events: Experienced visions since childhood, confirmed by theologians at 43
Elected magistra of Disibodenberg convent in 1136
Founded the monastery at Rupertsberg in 1150
Founded a second monastery at Eibingen in 1165
Canonized in 2012 and declared Doctor of the Church by Pope Benedict XVI
Notable_Contributions: Authored visionary works such as 'Scivias', 'Liber vitae meritorum', and 'Liber divinorum operum'
Composed sacred music, including the 'Symphonia armonie celestium revelationum'
Pioneered scientific natural history in Germany
Developed the constructed language 'Lingua Ignota'
Advocated for reform and unity within the Church
Quotes: The Word is living, being, spirit, all verdant greening, all creativity.
O fire of the Holy Spirit, life of the life of every creature, holy are you in giving life to forms.

Name: Saint Rocco
Major_Events: Distributed his wealth to the poor after the death of his parents
Traveled as a pilgrim curing plague victims in Italy and other regions
Miraculously survived his own battle with the plague in the forest with aid from a dog
Was imprisoned for five years as a suspected spy and died in prison
Notable_Contributions: Known for miraculous healings of plague victims through prayer and the sign of the cross
Venerated as a protector against plagues and contagious diseases
Inspired devotion and miracles associated with his relics after his death
Quotes: I am your nephew, Rocco.
